memory_update.text: Lincoln Educational Services and Universal Technical Institute are the clearest direct public-market proxies for employer-aligned vocational and skilled-trades training in this theme funnel.
Stride's career-training brands, especially MedCerts, are a useful second-order exposure because they connect online certification training to employer and workforce-agency demand.
Nelnet should be tracked as an adjacent education-payment and servicing rail rather than a direct training operator.
The market may under-map vocational operators as legacy education names even though the actual chokepoint is employer-certified technician capacity.

summary: Direct exposure is concentrated in specialized vocational operators that sell employer-certified technician capacity, not generic education. The strongest underfollowed names in this lane are Lincoln Educational Services and Universal Technical Institute, both of which show explicit employer/brand partnerships and campus-level workforce pipelines. Stride adds a blended online career-training angle through MedCerts, while Nelnet is a second-order beneficiary via education payment and servicing rails. The market may still under-map these businesses as legacy education names rather than capacity providers for employers with persistent skilled-labor shortages.
